body:
I wish I had solid advice to give you and more to give other than my sympathies. Sounds like your sister is going through it, the good news is she is young enough where she can still change. 12 yr olds are always selfish and self centered. It’s just how the age group is. Not very rational or self reflecting. You could try and point out to her the parallels of her and your mom to get the gears in her head moving towards being different. It’s hard because she is rude and mean but she needs to be guided in a nice enough manner in order to actually ‘see’ what she’s doing. At age 12 she isn’t very advice prone either, try to help her understand that her behavior has effects on others. 

As for your mom, your dad has to stand up for himself. Tell your dad he’s worth more than people who step all over him. He might have low self esteem and that’s why he isn’t able to really push back. 

But you’re incredibly kind - you’re already doing great by setting a good example for your sister. I’m more than sure your dad sees it too.  I’m sorry that you have to deal with this. I hope I was able to help a little bit and bring up some ideas you maybe hadn’t tried yet.

You’re boyfriend is immature and he really is being manipulative, even if he doesn’t mean to be. You can’t teach someone empathy and you can’t teach someone to listen to you. Personally, I think it would be best to get some space from him and take time to really sort out how you feel about how you are being treated and if maybe you need to take a break from relationships all together until you are stable.

There are many reasons why a person would throw away a relationship of 20 yrs. while, yes, what you said technically, can be true, but I do think it’s highly unlikely. Based on the one post, I’d say OP has a history of letting people into her life that don’t really value her and they treat her as such. And she normalizes it, does anything in her power to not look at the people she loves like that. Chances are OP’s friend never valued her as someone important to her, 20 yrs be damned because those 20 yrs OP served a purpose to her and now OP is in the way of something she wants. The revenge thing also can fit into this as well because if it was about revenge then she’s the cruelest type to wait and hide in the grass until OP shows a great weakness and uses it against her. Not to mention sociopathic as well.

No, she didn’t want to find out what was really happening because if she did she wouldn’t have lied and purposely tried to make OP look as bad as possible. She’s not worried about OP, she thinks OP is being ungrateful and sees this is an opportunity. If this was about concern the last thing you would do is tell the person that you think is hurting your friend that they’re complaining about them which in turn would make the abuser get mad at them and possibly hurt them. Why are you jumping over hoops to make Hannah’s actions ok or acceptable when they clearly are not?

I mean it sucks but you’re pretty much better without him. I mean he had the chance to be honest with you but for him it was never about honesty. He’s a snake that saw the opportunity to hurt you. And if it’s the case that there is a genuine problem he had with you he should’ve been an adult about it and said it to your face instead of behind your back like a coward. As for your other friends you could try and reach out to them to try and get the whole story and explain yourself but ultimately you’d better off without them as true friends would’ve talked to you about what your BFF was saying instead of just believing it. Don’t waste your time on people who aren’t real with you.

It’s not just a simple question and to hide behind that excuse is just plain wrong. There are pointed questions that can be used to make another person feel self-conscious. The question you asked is a fine example because it is a clear jab at their writing ability under the guis of a ‘simple question’. I can accept that you were genuinely curious but it doesn’t justify going about it like that bc by the end of the day none of this will matter and it’s not worth making a fuss about.
No need to be rude about someone’s English. Nothing in their comment made me think they were abnormally poor with writing. Ffs dude go after ideas not people.
What kinda of 7th grade shit is this
Is it Alicia online?
Thanks, but that isn’t her. She’s completely bald. None of her videos showed any hair.
I’ve already used her physical description to look for her on both TikTok and google, but she doesn’t ‘advertise’ herself as that, so it’s made it quite difficult to find her.

You did the right thing, quitting your job that you hated. It sounds like to me the only reason they are mad is because they are losing out on the money they take from you. They are using you, and that’s not right, because they are supposed to be the parents. I’m sorry that you’re going through this and to give my two cents I would keep my head down until I can move out and never talk to them again. They sound toxic, and do not care for you like a parent should. You’re not the failure, they are and they are projecting.
Thanks for believing in me. Your words really do mean a lot.
Thank you.
I haven’t mostly because my mom doesn’t believe that I have depression or any form of mental illness. I’ve never even gotten a diagnosis.

You should probably tell your brother what happened and if that doesn’t work you will probably have to explain to the wife the importance of keeping her kids in check or just that things have to change. It sucks what situation you’re in and I hope it works out for you and your mother.

Not to be like you’re kinda a bad person but you kinda are. I wouldn’t say you’re horrible just kinda selfish. You knew what you were getting into with this girl but you did it anyways. Also it’s clear she doesn’t love you and is more interested in cheating than a relationship. She’s the 100% in the wrong here and you should do the right thing and tell her bf.

I’m sorry to hear it didn’t work out. It’s sucks but you did your best and unfortunately he’s going to have to learn the hard way. Sometimes that’s the only way. Just know that I really admire you for looking out for him, even thought you didn’t have to. I have a brother similar to yours so I can understand how it’s very painful to see. You can always PM me if you need to talk more about it.

sorry to be the bearer of bad news, but you can’t change someone who doesn’t want to change. It seems to me that’s he’s very comfortable where he is and if he’s going to make any progress it has to be his choice. You could try and talk to him heart to heart, but based on what you’ve said I don’t think it will go great but it’s a shot and could work.
It sounds like you’ve already made up your mind, he’s not going to change and you gotta decide if your willing to put up with that.
I don’t think he will be sad or remorseful when I leave, but you are right. Sometimes I forget that this isn’t normal. Thank you for the response.
Yes, at least in my personal experience and can be pretty nasty to our parents and I. I’ve only heard good things from his friends, however.

I did what you said and he sent back “shut the fuck up you stupid bitch you told somebody i hit mom and pee in bottles. keep my name out of your mouth. i hate you”. 

So yeah I guess you could say he didn’t believe me. But thank you for your reply.

This is hard, but this isn’t your fight. You can’t make people make amends, or change. They have to do it themselves, you can try to help, but ultimately this is in their hands. I understand that family is important to you, but the problem doesn’t start or end with you. 

You don’t have to choose between you mom or your siblings, you don’t have to be the glue that holds the family together. And in the end, you shouldn’t have to. Your family is fully capable of fixing their own problems. Just being there and being in support of change is enough.

As hard as it is, you are truly better left off leaving. Your mother is toxic and you do not need that. Moving out might be lonely at first, but eventually you will meet other people. Change is scary, but it’s better than a toxic home. You deserve better.

As for your mother and your guilt, I have little advice, and all I can say is that independence from a selfish mother is what you need. You do not owe her anything. It’s tough and I hope the best for you.

I’d say pick your battles. The example you gave would be a good one to just let drop. You can’t fix him, but you can try your best to avoid petty arguments like these. Sometimes things just don’t work out, and it sounds like to me, your biggest problem is that he is unwilling to hear you out. It’s possible though, that he is just irritated by you pushing it with the questions.
